companyDescription: Lunar Infrastructure + NASA CLPS Services · Nova-C/Nova-D landers, $1.1B+ backlog across IM-3/IM-4/IM-5 — lost the NASA Lunar Terrain Vehicle rover contract in May 2026, now a lander/services pure-play rather than a multi-program mobility platform
priceNote: $15.14, down ~68% from the May 29 all-time high of $46.75. Two real negatives since the last report: NASA awarded the Lunar Terrain Vehicle contract to Astrolab/Lunar Outpost (not LUNR) in May, and a $500M ATM equity program launched Jun 2 is an ongoing dilution overhang — the primary driver of a 7-day, -24.5% losing streak into mid-Jul. IM-3 (H2 2026) has NOT launched yet.
marketCap: ~$3.3B (est. — ATM issuance ongoing, share count in flux)
summary: Intuitive Machines lost the NASA Lunar Terrain Vehicle award to Astrolab ($219M) and Lunar Outpost ($220M) in May 2026, ending its bid to be a multi-program Artemis mobility prime, and launched a $500M ATM equity program on Jun 2 that's created a real, ongoing dilution overhang — together explaining most of the -68% drawdown from May's ATH. These are realized setbacks, not just sentiment. Against that: backlog is still $1.1B+, a fresh $148.3M NASA lander contract landed Jul 1, IM-3 (targeting Reiner Gamma, H2 2026) has not launched yet and remains a live catalyst, and Craig-Hallum reiterated Buy through the decline. This is a wide-dispersion, binary-catalyst speculative name, not a clean buy-the-dip.

catalysts.name: IM-3 Lunar Mission — Reiner Gamma
catalysts.description: Third Nova-C lander mission, targeting the Reiner Gamma region — has NOT launched as of mid-Jul despite some stale coverage implying otherwise. Redundant altimeters + lighting-independent navigation sensors target the upright-landing failures that hit IM-1 and IM-2. Exact launch date not yet set; NASA/company guidance says second half 2026.

catalysts.name: Q2 2026 Earnings
catalysts.description: Consensus-estimated date, not yet officially confirmed by IR. Key reads: revenue trajectory off Q1's $186.7M, commentary on ATM pace/dilution, and any guidance revision following the LTV contract loss.

catalysts.name: NASA $148.3M Nova-C Production Lander Contract
catalysts.description: Jul 1, 2026: NASA awarded up to $148.3M for a production-line-qualified Nova-C lander (Moon delivery by 2028). Extends backlog and partially offsets the narrative damage from May's LTV-contract miss.

risks: REALIZED: NASA awarded the Lunar Terrain Vehicle contract to Astrolab ($219M) and Lunar Outpost ($220M) in May 2026 — LUNR was not selected despite winning an earlier $30M Phase 1 feasibility award; no longer positioned as an Artemis rover prime

REALIZED: $500M at-the-market equity program launched Jun 2, 2026 — an ongoing dilution overhang (not a one-time event) that is the primary driver of the stock's decline and will keep pressuring shares until the program is exhausted or capped
Track record: IM-1 tipped on landing (Feb 2024), IM-2 landed on its side with limited data transmission (Mar 2025) — IM-3's upright landing is not guaranteed despite hardware fixes
Technical damage: 7 consecutive down days into mid-Jul, trading well below its 200-day moving average
Customer/NASA budget concentration — Congressional funding risk to the CLPS program this backlog depends on

catalystSpot.preRunup: LUNR has historically run 20-30% in the weeks before a confirmed lunar mission launch window as retail/institutional buyers front-run mission excitement. That pattern is likely muted this cycle given the active $500M ATM program can absorb/cap any pre-launch rally.

postWin.note: IM-1 (Feb 2024), the first private Moon landing, drove +45% in 3 days despite a partial tip-over. Even the smaller NASA LRO Camera contract win drove +14.6% in May 2026 — shows sensitivity to positive NASA news at these suppressed levels.

postLose.note: The Jun 2 ATM announcement itself triggered persistent selling (part of the subsequent 7-day, -24.5% losing streak) — a genuine dilution overhang, not short-lived fear. A failed IM-3 landing would likely compound this.

spotSizing.reason: Two real negative catalysts (LTV loss, $500M ATM) have realized since the prior report — smaller sizing than before is warranted despite the backlog/analyst-target upside. Treat as a small speculative allocation pending IM-3 clarity or ATM resolution. Max 5% of portfolio.

comparableCases.event: IM-1 first private Moon landing validation
comparableCases.note: LUNR's own IM-1 drove +45% in 3 days despite a partial tip-over on landing — mission declared partially successful. A clean IM-3 landing could produce a larger move from today's much lower base.

Even a $20M recurring services contract drove +14.6% — the market is sensitive to positive NASA news at current suppressed levels, which argues the $148.3M Jul 1 contract is a real (if partial) offset to the LTV loss.

Stock kept falling after the ATM launch as investors priced in ongoing share issuance — a genuine, still-unresolved dilution overhang, and the direct precursor to the 7-day losing streak that followed into mid-Jul.
